title: First trip to Los Angeles and the Dunbar Hotel
summary: Greer recalls filming Check and Double Check, an earthquake and the song 'Hi, Sue'.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Now we've switched, we're going to talk about Los Angeles. Go ahead.
We went out, the first time I went to Los Angeles we went out to make the picture --

And Murder at the Vanities. And I went out there, man, sun was shining, everybody out there playing that miniature golf and everything was beautiful. So I said, boy, this is -- I called New York, I called my father. I say, "This is it. Sell the house and come out here." He say, "No." Man, we was in the hotel, the Dunbar. You remember the Dunbar Hotel on Central Avenue?

Yeah, we were in the Dunbar. We were living there. So the hotel got to shaking one morning, early. I was downstairs in the shooting gallery, because (inaudible) down there getting an eye-opener. Man, one of them light tremors -- one of them heavy tremors. Ray Nance got downstairs in the lobby of this hotel with only his shorts on. I said, "Man, where are you going?" He said, "Man, the world's coming to an end." I said, "Man, it's okay." Had to take a lot of people to talk to him, he was so scared. But I'm (inaudible) don't pay it no mind.

So we used to go out, the studio would send a driver for us. Come out -- because that's a long ways out to Hollywood from Central Avenue. We had to go out early. So we were riding around, riding around. And you know, the car stopped -- the bus stops in California, they sit on the side. So we were riding along and I'm sitting at the window and I lean out and just said to women going to work, "Hi, Sue."

Right away Duke say, "Man, that's a title for a song." And he wrote it. "Hi, Sue." We recorded it. "Hi, Sue." That's right. So we get on the set and we were making -- you know, we were making this Amos and Andy thing first and they were --(Freeman and) Gosden and them were very good friends of mine. And so they said, "Hey, Sonny, how you feel?" I said, "Terrible". They said, "Come on, Man, we have a little taste on after work."
What were some songs from that picture?
I don't think they had a hit song in that picture. But we made the picture anyhow. They were very nice. So then we go from there to Murder at the Vanities, you know. So I think I told you about that.
